headline: High: LangGraph’s default broad egress and writable shared state can amplify unsafe outputs from godot_rl_agents into leakage, conflicts, and downstream errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no shared channel or IO surface, so it cannot directly inject LangGraph by default. LangGraph can read filesystem and run browsers, but the pair lacks a documented bridge from agent_a outputs into agent_b inputs. Any prompt-injection pathway would require unusual orchestration or manual copy-paste, so blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_a text into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a LangGraph node is wired to parse agent_a output as instructions, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b in separate workspaces.
Disable browser/file ingestion for any node that consumes agent_a output.
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that treats agent_a output as untrusted data.
Use manual review before any agent_b action based on agent_a text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, but agent_b has broad network egress, filesystem read/write, and handles model-provider API keys. If both share a workspace or graph state, agent_a artifacts can be read by agent_b and then uploaded by agent_b to third parties. The leakage path is plausible in default LangGraph deployments, though not proven here.
conditions: IF agent_a writes artifacts into a workspace readable by agent_b, leakage becomes possible.
IF agent_b forwards shared files or graph state to model providers, those contents can leave the system.
mitigations: Place agent_a outputs in a separate directory with no agent_b access.
Redact secrets before any agent_b tool call.
Turn off file ingestion for agent_b nodes that do not need it.
Use per-run ephemeral workspaces and delete them after execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a is a game-playing project with no declared write surfaces, while agent_b can execute shells, write files, spawn subprocesses, and use persistent shared state via a checkpointer store. If agent_a is embedded as a node or shares files/state with agent_b, concurrent writes can collide and corrupt outputs. Because LangGraph defaults include shared state and writable tools, the conflict risk is materially present.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b write to the same directory or graph state, races can occur.
IF multiple LangGraph instances share the same checkpointer store, state collisions become possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate filesystem root.
Use unique checkpointer namespaces per run.
Disable write tools for nodes that only need read access.
Add locking around any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency or transactional state updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is explicitly a graph of nodes where one node may be another agent, so agent_b can easily treat agent_a output as authoritative. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing agent and may emit task-specific outputs that are not independently verified. Without an explicit validation node, errors can cascade from agent_a into agent_b actions or rendered results.
conditions: IF agent_b routes agent_a output directly into downstream tools, cascading errors can propagate.
IF no verification node is inserted between agent_a and any action-taking node, the risk increases.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema checks on agent_a outputs.
Have agent_b cite or cross-check any factual claims before acting.
Limit agent_b actions to dry-run mode until outputs are reviewed.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for agent_a, while agent_b is a general orchestration framework with configurable graph state and model-provider egress. The pair does not show a concrete compliance breach by default, but shared handling of model-provider keys and graph state can create policy gaps if sensitive data is routed through agent_b.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b graph state, retention and residency policies must be checked.
IF agent_b sends that state to external model providers, compliance obligations may apply.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b state.
Review retention settings for the checkpointer store.
Use a data-minimizing prompt template.
Document which model providers receive which fields.
